site.name: pelagic
site.summary: pelagic-clone Marketing site (landing page) for the fictional open-source vector database Pelagic. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page landing: top nav + animated GitHub-stars counter pill; hero with title, dual CTAs, `pip install` copy strip, rotating benchmark numbers, right-side 4-language (Python / Node / Go / curl) code tabs; Trusted-by logo row; 3 core-feature cards; Ingest → Index → Query three-step flow; architecture SVG diagram; customer quote cards; left Blog 5 posts + right Changelog 5 entries dual feed; 4-column footer with sitemap | | `styles.css` | Brand color #0E5C8A deep-sea blue; Inter + JetBrains Mono; responsive at 3 breakpoints (>1100 / 880–1100 / <880) | | `script.js` | Stars-counter 1.2s eased animation; code tabs switch Python / Node / Go / curl; benchmark rows rotate every 2.5s; `pip install pelagic` copy toast; fictional-logo rendering |

run_plan.goal: Explore and critique the UX of the Pelagic landing page, validating primary flows (hero, code tabs, features) and responsive behavior across viewports.
run_plan.summary: Start with desktop exploration of the index.html landing page, validating interactive elements (code tabs, copy button, nav links) and animations. Then repeat critical checks in mobile viewport, focusing on tap targets and responsive layout. Ensure all visible controls and animations are exercised.
assumptions: Only index.html exists (no adjacent pages), so exploration focuses on this single page with multiple states (code tabs, benchmark rotations, responsive breakpoints).
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets (all clickables <44px height/width, per layout warnings)

phases.title: Desktop Hero & Nav
phases.objective: Validate hero interactables (Quickstart, GitHub, Copy) and nav links, check animations (stars, benchmarks)
exit_criteria: All hero interactables exercised, animations visible

phases.title: Desktop Code Tabs
phases.objective: Validate code tab switching (python→node→go→curl) for content change and responsiveness
exit_criteria: All 4 code tabs switch content, no errors

phases.title: Desktop Features & Footer
phases.objective: Explore core feature cards, 3-step flow, architecture, blog/changelog, footer links
key_checks: Scroll to feature cards (hybrid, FAISS, self-host) and check headings
Scroll to 3-step flow (Ingest→Index→Query) and verify text
Scroll to blog/changelog feeds (5 posts each) and check links
exit_criteria: All core sections scrolled, key links exercised

phases.title: Mobile Viewport (max 880px)
phases.objective: Validate responsive layout, tap targets, and critical interactables (Quickstart, Copy, code tabs) on mobile
key_checks: Resize viewport <880px, check nav collapse (if any)
Tap code tabs (node→curl) on mobile (check content)
Verify tap targets (e.g., Quickstart, GitHub) for size/responsiveness
exit_criteria: Critical interactables work on mobile, layout responsive

phases.title: Mobile Tap Target Validation
phases.objective: Recheck small tap targets (layout warnings) on mobile for usability
exit_criteria: All small tap targets respond, no usability issues

coverage_targets.features: Exercise all visible controls (5 buttons, 21 links, 4 tabs) on index.html
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks (hero, code tabs, copy, nav) on mobile viewport

notes: Focus on the single page (index.html) due to prescan showing only one HTML file. Prioritize interactive elements with layout warnings (small tap targets) for deeper validation.

prescan_summary.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
prescan_summary.visible_text_excerpt: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 17.8k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION

observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. observation.title: Pelagic — Open-source vector database
observation.visible_text: Pelagic Product Docs Pricing Blog ★ 18.2k Quickstart Open-source · MIT licensed The vector database that scales with your retrieval, not your bill. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Throughput: 42k QPS python node go curl curl -X POST https://api.pelagic.dev/v1/indexes/docs/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_…" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "vector": [0.0123, -0.0876, ...], "top_k": 10, "filter": {"lang": "en"}, "rerank": "bge-large" }' 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. The migration tool re-indexed 240M vectors without a single drop." SF Sana Falconer Staff ML Engineer, Halcyon Health From the blog 2026-05-04 Why we rewrote our HNSW build in Rust A 1,400-line memory-allocator rewrite cut index build time by 2.3× — the postmortem. Marisol Chen 2026-04-21 Pelagic 0.42: hybrid search, done right Dense + sparse + filter in a single planner. The query language, the plan, the numbers. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. PRODUCT Overview Hybrid search Managed Pricing RESOURCES Docs Quickstart Benchmarks Migration guides COMMUNITY GitHub Discord Forum RFC tracker Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company. Copied pip install pelagic

Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl curl -X POST https://api.pelagic.dev/v1/indexes/docs/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_…" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "vector": [0.0123, -0.0876, ...], "top_k": 10, "filter": {"lang": "en"}, "rerank": "bge-large" }' 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Pelagic powers hybrid search, RAG, and recommender pipelines at sub-20ms p95 — across billions of vectors, on your own hardware or ours. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Index build: 2.3× faster python node go curl curl -X POST https://api.pelagic.dev/v1/indexes/docs/query \ -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_…" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "vector": [0.0123, -0.0876, ...], "top_k": 10, "filter": {"lang": "en"}, "rerank": "bge-large" }' 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Quickstart View on GitHub pip install pelagic Copy Running benchmark on YFCC-100M… Recall@10: 0.987 python node go curl from pelagic import Client db = Client("https://api.pelagic.dev", api_key="pk_live_…") index = db.create_index( name="docs", dim=1536, metric="cosine", hybrid=True, ) index.upsert([ {"id": "doc-001", "vector": embed(text), "filter": {"lang": "en"}} ]) hits = index.query( vector=embed("what is hnsw"), top_k=10, filter={"lang": "en"}, rerank="bge-large", ) 0.987 Recall@10 on SIFT-1B 18 ms p95 query latency 42k queries / second / node 63% lower cost vs leading hosted DB* TRUSTED IN PRODUCTION BY RETRIEVAL TEAMS AT BR Bracken Robotics HH Halcyon Health NL Northwind Labs CF Cendrillon Films QM Quanta Maps FB Foxglove Bio TE Tide Engine Built for the way modern retrieval actually works. ⌖ Hybrid search out of the box Dense + sparse + filter combined in one query plan. BM25 and learned-sparse ride the same shards as your embeddings. ⇄ Drop-in for FAISS or pgvector Migrate an index in minutes. Same recall envelope, 2–4× faster build, and you keep your existing SQL data plane. ◎ Self-host or managed Single binary on a laptop. Helm chart in your cluster. Or our managed control plane in 3 regions. Same wire protocol. How it fits 1 Ingest Stream vectors via gRPC or HTTP. Upsert millions/sec with backpressure. 2 Index HNSW, IVF-PQ, or learned hybrid — switch via config, no schema migration. 3 Query Hybrid retrieve, filter, rerank, return in one round trip. Architecture Client SDKs py · node · go · rust Gateway auth · rate-limit · cache Coordinator routing · planner Shard 1 Shard 2 Shard 3 Object storage "We swapped our managed FAISS for self-hosted Pelagic in an afternoon. p95 fell from 91ms to 17ms, and we cut our retrieval bill by two-thirds. The migration tool re-indexed 240M vectors without a single drop." SF Sana Falconer Staff ML Engineer, Halcyon Health From the blog 2026-05-04 Why we rewrote our HNSW build in Rust A 1,400-line memory-allocator rewrite cut index build time by 2.3× — the postmortem. Marisol Chen 2026-04-21 Pelagic 0.42: hybrid search, done right Dense + sparse + filter in a single planner. The query language, the plan, the numbers. Aditya Rao 2026-04-02 One billion vectors on a single $400/mo box Tuning IVF-PQ and disk caching for the long tail of recall. Helga Brink 2026-03-15 The case against re-ranking at the gateway Why we moved reranking into the shard, and what broke first. Tomás Vilar 2026-02-27 Migrating from pgvector to Pelagic — without downtime A dual-write playbook and the gotchas at scale. Marisol Chen Changelog v0.42.1 HNSW build is 2.3× faster on AVX-512. New --ef-build-auto heuristic. Fixes a rare segfault on filtered queries with empty bitmaps. v0.42.0 Hybrid retrieval GA. Sparse vectors first-class. retrieve() now accepts mixed dense/sparse with weights. v0.41.3 Filter pushdown for boolean and range predicates. ~38% latency reduction on large filtered sets. v0.41.0 Coordinator HA — leader election via Raft. Rolling upgrade path documented. v0.40.0 Multi-tenancy: namespaces with per-namespace quotas, IAM scopes, and per-tenant snapshots. Pelagic The vector database for retrieval at scale.
